pages.title: Journal of Contemporary Eastern Asia
pages.html:
Journal of Contemporary Eastern Asia (JCEA)

ISSN 2383-9449 · A peer-reviewed journal on convergence and future studies in Asia, published biannually.

The Journal of Contemporary Eastern Asia publishes peer-reviewed scholarship on East Asia, data, and the networked society. Originally focused on political, social, and economic trends in East and Southeast Asia, the journal has evolved to emphasize (socio-technical) convergence and future (network) studies.

Open Access

All content is freely available without charge to the user or their institution. Readers may read, download, copy, distribute, print, search, or link to the full texts of articles without prior permission. Articles are published under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs 3.0 Unported license.

Announcements

  • Call for Papers: Special issue on Living with ChatGPT: Social, Psychological, and Economic Impacts of Generative AI in East Asia — abstracts due November 30, 2025.
  • Conference: Triple Helix Conference 2025, 28–31 October 2025, Tecnologico de Monterrey, Monterrey, Mexico.
  • Best Paper Awards: JCEA recognizes the most outstanding papers published in the journal each year, selected by the editorial board.

Recent Issues

  • Vol. 25, No. 1 (Summer 2026): Eight articles on topics including AI adoption in FinTech, financial leverage, entertainment celebrity conversions, monetary dynamics in Nepal, digital resistance through memes in China, Weibo information satisfaction, green finance policies in Indonesia, and Filipino migration to South Korea.
  • Vol. 24, No. 2 (Winter 2025): Ten articles addressing digital signage and social media, Palestinian-Israeli representation in Korean news, digital piracy frameworks, political expression analysis, privacy vulnerabilities in digital China, video games and digital diplomacy, unlicensed game access in China, and Taiwan's COVID-19 digital response.
  • Vol. 24, No. 1 (Summer 2025): Six research articles covering agrarian perspectives on Indonesian capital development, media credibility and political participation, state media trust in China, Korean Wave perception in Vietnam, humanitarian aid diplomacy, and Indonesian migrant entrepreneurship in Japan.

pages.title: About the Journal
pages.html:
About the Journal

The Journal of Contemporary Eastern Asia (JCEA), ISSN 2383-9449, publishes peer-reviewed scholarship on East Asia, data, and the networked society. It is a biannual journal on convergence and future studies in Asia.

Aims and Scope

The journal originally covered political, social, and economic trends in East and Southeast Asia, and has since broadened its focus to socio-technical convergence and future network studies. JCEA welcomes original research as well as significant reexaminations of existing literature.

History

  • 2001: Founded by the Austrian Association of East Asian Studies together with scholars from Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea.
  • 2010: The Cyber Emotions Research Center at YeungNam University became co-publisher alongside WATEF.
  • After 2012: Following the Austrian Association's closure during the European financial crisis, JCEA transferred to YeungNam University's Cyber Emotions Research Center and the Asia Triple Helix Society (renamed WATEF in 2015).

Publisher

JCEA is published by the Cyber Emotions Research Center, YeungNam University (Korea) and WATEF (World Association for Triple Helix and Future Strategy Studies).

Open Access

All content is freely available without charge to the user or his/her institution. Users may read, download, copy, distribute, print, search, or link to the full texts of articles without prior permission.

Indexing

The journal is listed in Scopus and DOAJ, among other databases.

pages.title: Editorial Process
pages.html:
Editorial Process

JCEA follows a rigorous, multi-stage editorial process for all submitted manuscripts.

1. Pre-check

A managing editor assesses the manuscript's suitability for the journal and the qualifications of the authors, and rejects obviously substandard submissions. The Academic Editor is notified and invited to recommend reviewers.

2. Peer Review

At least two review reports are collected for each submitted article. JCEA uses single-blind review: authors do not know the reviewers' identities, but reviewers know the authors' identities. All reviewers must:

  • Hold no conflicts of interest with the authors
  • Possess a PhD
  • Have recent publications in the field of the submitted paper
  • Not have recently reviewed for JCEA journals

Reviewers are given two weeks to write their review. For the review of a revised manuscript, reviewers are asked to provide their report within three days. The full peer-review process typically takes approximately two months.

3. Editor Decision

Editors evaluate reviewer suitability, the adequacy of reviewer comments, and the scientific quality of the work. Decision options include accept, reject, request revisions, or seek additional reviewers.

4. Revision

Authors typically revise before further external review referral. Apart from exceptional circumstances, a maximum of two rounds of major revision per manuscript is allowed.

5. Production

Accepted papers undergo professional language editing, copy editing, and XML conversion. Author fees may apply for extensive editing work.

Publication Ethics

JCEA is a member of the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) and follows its procedures for handling unethical behavior. The journal also follows CONSORT, TOP, and ACOMS guidelines.

pages.title: Submission Guidelines
pages.html:
Submission Guidelines

How to Submit

All submissions must be made through the online editorial system at ACOMS+. For technical issues with the system, contact acomsplus@kisti.re.kr; for questions about the submission process, contact j.c.eastern.asia@gmail.com.

Article Processing Charges (APC)

  • USD 100 (KRW 150,000) for all authors, payable upon acceptance.
  • For funded research, an additional fee of USD 200 (KRW 300,000) applies, bringing the total to USD 300 (KRW 450,000).
  • JCEA Associate Editors and invited scholars are exempt for up to one unfunded publication per year.

Manuscript Types and Word Limits

  • Full-length research papers: maximum 8,000 words, including abstract and bibliography
  • Short research / rapid communications: 2,000–3,000 words, focusing on preliminary results and novel ideas
  • Book reviews: maximum 5,000 words
  • Editor's notes: three to ten pages

Format Requirements

Submissions must be in Microsoft Word or RTF format and must follow the manuscript template for in-text citations, reference lists, headings, and other formatting. Non-compliant manuscripts are automatically rejected.

Pre-submission Checklist

  • Correct file format and adherence to word limits
  • Template compliance for citations and formatting
  • Copyright compliance, with proper citations for any previously published material
  • A cover letter with the names and contact information of all authors, a research summary, an originality statement, and the names of three experts in your area with affiliations and rationale for recommendation
  • A plagiarism check report from Grammarly, Turnitin, or another international plagiarism checker

Copyright and Licensing

Authors retain copyright and grant the journal right of first publication. Work is distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution-No Derivative Works License. Authors may post their work to institutional repositories with proper attribution to its initial publication in JCEA.

Ethics and Timeline

The journal adheres to Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) guidelines. The peer-review process typically takes approximately two months.

pages.title: Abstracting and Indexing
pages.html:
Abstracting and Indexing

Make your research known. The Journal of Contemporary Eastern Asia is indexed and abstracted in the following databases:

  • Scopus
  • EBSCOhost
  • Google Scholar
  • DOAJ (Directory of Open Access Journals)

Indexing ensures that peer-reviewed scholarship on East Asia, data, and the networked society published in JCEA reaches a broad international audience.

pages.title: Copyright and Authors' Responsibilities
pages.html:
Copyright and Authors' Responsibilities

License

All articles are published under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivs 3.0 (CC BY-NC-ND 3.0) license.

Copyright Ownership

Authors retain copyright and grant JCEA the right of first publication in print and online. The work is distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution-No Derivative Works License.

Permitted Uses

  • The work may be shared with an acknowledgement of the work's authorship and initial publication in the Journal of Contemporary Eastern Asia.
  • Attribution is required in both electronic and paper formats.

Restrictions

  • The work may not be altered or transformed.
  • You may not alter, transform, or build upon this work.

Secondary Distribution

Authors may enter into separate, additional contractual arrangements for the non-exclusive distribution of the journal's published version (for example, posting to an institutional repository or including it in a book), with proper acknowledgement of its initial publication in JCEA. The journal would appreciate notification of reproductions at j.c.eastern.asia[at]gmail.com.

Jurisdiction and Privacy

The court of jurisdiction is Daegu, Republic of Korea. Names and email addresses entered on the journal site are used exclusively for the stated purposes of this journal and will not be made available for any other purpose.

pages.title: Call for Papers: Living with ChatGPT (Special Issue)
pages.html:
Call for Papers — Special Issue

Living with ChatGPT: Social, Psychological, and Economic Impacts of Generative AI in East Asia

Guest Editors: Dr. Weiwen Yu (Arizona State University) and Dr. Chun Shao (Marquette University)

This special issue examines how generative AI tools have transformed technology engagement, particularly following ChatGPT's release in 2022. It focuses on East Asian contexts, including China's regulatory environment, Japan's emphasis on human–machine harmony, and South Korea's digital labor markets.

Topics of Interest

  • AI in educational settings and academic integrity
  • Generative AI within creative industries
  • Language, translation, and cultural considerations in AI output
  • Economic effects including automation and labor changes
  • AI-assisted emotional support and social applications
  • Public perception and regulatory discussions
  • User adaptation and creative uses of AI tools
  • Regional adoption variations across East Asia

How to Submit

Send abstracts (maximum 500 words) to both Dr. Yu (weiwenyu@asu.edu) and Dr. Shao (chun.shao@marquette.edu), copying j.c.eastern.asia@gmail.com. Include “JCEA Special Issue” in the subject line.

Timeline

  • Abstract deadline: November 30, 2025
  • Full paper invitations: December 15, 2025
  • Manuscript deadline: May 15, 2026

Publication Fees

USD 100 standard APC; an additional USD 200 applies for funded research. Associate editors receive one annual exemption for unfunded work.
